title: STORK: Faster Diffusion and Flow Matching Sampling by Resolving both Stiffness and Structure-Dependence
claim: At very low step budgets, baseline fast samplers produce flawed outputs, while ours yields more faithful, detailed samples that follow the prompt.
layout: 4 rows by 4 columns grid, with method names across the top and baselines left to right ending in ours; prompt in monospace and a one-line commentary under each row
description: A tall grid of generated images with four rows and four columns. Column headers read Flow-Euler, Flow-DPM-Solver++, Flow-UniPC and STORK (Ours), the last in bold. Each row is one text prompt, shown in monospace beneath the images. A serif commentary line follows it and says why the rightmost image is better. Row 1 is a cyberpunk stork holding a plaque, where baselines garble the text 'STORK' and ours spells it correctly. Row 2 is a cowboy singer on a horse, where baselines are dark and ours has a vivid, realistic background. caption: Comparison between the Flow-Euler, Flow-DPM-Solver++ [ref], Flow-UniPC [ref], and STORK. All images are generated using the SANA 1.6B model [ref] at $1024\times 1024$ resolution with only 8 NFEs. Prompts are displayed beneath each image pair, accompanied by our commentary explaining why STORK's generations are superior. STORK achieves much better visual fidelity at the extremely low NFE case, showing its effectiveness as a fast sampling method. Zoom in for better visual details.
abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) and flow-matching models have demonstrated remarkable performance in image and video generation. However, such models require a significant number of function evaluations (NFEs) during sampling, leading to costly inference. Consequently, quality-preserving fast sampling methods that require fewer NFEs have been an active area of research. However, prior training-free sampling methods fail to simultaneously address two key challenges: the stiffness of the ODE (i.e., the non-straightness of the velocity field) and dependence on the semi-linear structure of the DM ODE (which limits their direct applicability to flow-matching models). In this work, we introduce the Stabilized Taylor Orthogonal Runge--Kutta (STORK) method, addressing both design concerns. We demonstrate that STORK consistently improves the quality of diffusion and flow-matching sampling for image and video generation. Code is available at https://github.com/ZT220501/STORK.
